name: Nicola Paro
bio: Nicola Paro is a Solution Architect with over 10 years of experience in the industry, with a special focus on the Industrial IoT environment. He is passionate about software development, primarily using .NET, Blazor, and AI technologies.

bio: Software developer, MSc student of Computer Science & IT

name: Ratko Ćosić
bio: Ratko Ćosić is a seasoned application architect and tech lead with over 25 years of experience in building Microsoft‑based business systems. He works with C#/.NET, cloud‑native architectures, and Blazor/SPAs, delivering solutions across multiple industries. As a CTO, he leads distributed cloud, IoT, and AI projects, mentors engineering teams, and speaks at numerous regional and international conferences.

name: Žan Pokeržnik
bio: I’m a software engineer based in Slovenia with a strong background in .NET and C#, backend development, data-intensive systems, and system integrations. I enjoy solving complex technical problems and turning ideas into practical, production-ready software.

My experience includes large-scale data migrations, enterprise systems, and building reliable backend solutions. Alongside my engineering career, I run OrganizeIT, developing custom software and products such as MojeVabilo and OrganizeIT Checkout, focused on event digitalization, ticket sales, and payment workflows.

My technical interests include software architecture, backend engineering, database design, automation, and developer productivity. While .NET and C# have been a major part of my journey, I also enjoy exploring other technologies and am currently expanding my experience with Java and Quarkus.

name: Tomaž Koritnik
bio: I’m a curious, analytical, and solution-oriented thinker who enjoys turning complex challenges into elegant, practical solutions. I believe great software should be simple, understandable, maintainable, and built to evolve.

My approach combines technical excellence, creativity, and pragmatic software architecture. Software engineering is a continuous journey of learning, experimenting, and building things that make a difference.
topics: Software architecture and managing the complexity
